settings.aspect_ratio: Auto (disabled by UI with reference video)

prompt:
Create a fresh five-second continuous photorealistic shot for AFTERHUMAN. Image 3 (shot-02-v02) defines the exact extreme close-up composition, shirt, badge and lighting. Image 1 (badge-02-v01) is the exact flat badge artwork. Image 4 (riley-01-v01) supplies identity for the small PRINTED employee portrait only. Image 2 (badge-04-v01) defines the physical clear rigid badge holder, metal swivel and burgundy lanyard construction. Generate one continuous 16:9 shot, not a montage.

Video 1 (badge-motion-3s-v01.mp4) is the user's three-second recorded MOTION reference. Follow its real-time vertical bounce, small twists, perspective changes, pendulum motion, inertial lag and strap-to-holder timing. Use its motion at the supplied playback speed; do not stretch three seconds into five or slow it down. Continue that same natural movement seamlessly through the full five-second output, without a loop jump, freeze or restart. Transfer motion only: do not copy the recording's blue shirt, blank card, beige holder, room, body proportions or tight bottom-edge crop. The four still images above control Riley's appearance, badge hardware, print, framing and station lighting. Keep the complete holder visible with a little bottom margin throughout.

Riley is already running briskly on the first frame and continues at constant ordinary human pace. The camera follows her torso while the badge fills about 80 percent of frame height. The rigid rectangular badge follows Video 1's bounce and small twists, with natural inertia lag and light taps against her white shirt. The connected metal swivel and burgundy strap visibly carry its weight. Plausible motion only: no detached clip, floating holder, full spinning, duplicated badge or bending plastic.

Preserve the exact static printed artwork: KORVEX, Riley Brooks, EMPLOYEE, with the same layout and portrait. The printed face remains a motionless photograph, never a live animated face. Keep lettering sharp and stable rather than morphing. Reflections move over the transparent plastic naturally without replacing the print. Preserve the burgundy lanyard and morning cyan/magenta station reflections.

Maintain this extreme close-up throughout; no live face, waist, hands or bag enter frame. No cuts, slow motion, speed ramps, captions, HUD or implants.

Native audio: restrained train/station rumble, small plastic taps and fabric rustle. No spoken words, reading the badge, narration, singing or music.
